n: The Philistines gather for a major war against Israel. Achish tells David that he and his men must fight with the Philistine army — putting David in a terrible bind.

f.g: You must certainly understand.

n: David gives an ambiguous answer: “You will see what your servant can do.” Achish takes it as loyalty and makes David his permanent bodyguard.

f.g: bodyguard

n: The narrator sets the scene: Samuel is dead and buried, and Saul had earlier removed mediums and spiritists from the land, as God's law required.

f.g: Mediums who claimed to communicate with the dead.
spiritists, fortune-tellers

n: The Philistines camp at Shunem in the Jezreel Valley; Saul gathers Israel on Mount Gilboa across the valley. The stage is set for Saul's last battle.

f.g: A town in the Jezreel Valley in northern Israel.
A mountain ridge on the southeast side of the Jezreel Valley.

n: Seeing the Philistine army, Saul is terrified, his heart trembling. The man who once led Israel boldly is now ruled by fear.
Saul asks the Lord for guidance, but receives no answer — no dreams, no Urim, no prophets. Having repeatedly rejected God's word, Saul finds the heavens silent.

f.g: Part of the sacred Urim and Thummim used to receive revelation.

n: In desperation Saul orders his servants to find a medium — breaking his own law and God's. They point him to a woman at En-dor.

f.g: A village near Mount Tabor, behind the Philistine lines from Gilboa.

n: Saul disguises himself, goes by night with two men, and asks the woman to call up someone he will name. The king sneaks in the dark to do what he once condemned.

f.g: use your occult arts to tell me

n: The woman suspects a trap, reminding him that Saul has banned mediums. Why is he trying to get her killed?

f.w: layest thou a snare for my life
f.g: are you setting a trap to get me killed?

n: Saul swears by the Lord that she won't be punished — using God's name to protect a practice God forbids. A sad irony.
She asks whom to call, and Saul says, “Samuel.” He turns to the dead prophet whose living counsel he ignored.
When the woman sees a figure she identifies as Samuel, she screams — apparently something unexpected happens — and she realizes her visitor is Saul himself.

f.g: Her shock suggests this was not her usual experience.

n: Saul tells her not to fear and asks what she sees. She describes a godlike being rising from the earth.

f.g: Hebrew elohim — here a spirit being or supernatural figure.

n: She describes an old man wrapped in a robe. Saul concludes it is Samuel and bows to the ground. Note that Saul himself apparently sees nothing.

f.g: robe — perhaps recalling the robe Saul once tore

n: The figure asks why Saul has disturbed him. Saul pours out his distress: the Philistines are attacking, and God won't answer him. Readers differ on this scene: some believe God allowed Samuel to speak; many Latter-day Saint teachers have doubted a medium could summon a prophet.

f.g: disturbed

n: The answer is blunt: why ask me, if the Lord has left you and become your enemy? No other source can replace the Lord's guidance.
The Lord has done exactly what He said through Samuel: torn the kingdom from Saul and given it to David.

f.w: rent the kingdom out of thine hand

n: The reason is restated: Saul disobeyed the Lord regarding Amalek. That moment of disobedience defined his reign.
The message ends with doom: Israel will fall to the Philistines, and tomorrow Saul and his sons will join the dead.

f.w: to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me
f.g: That is, among the dead.

n: Saul collapses full length on the ground, overwhelmed with fear and weakened by having fasted all day and night.

f.w: fell straightway all along on the earth
f.g: fell flat on the ground

n: The woman sees how shaken Saul is and reminds him that she risked her life to do what he asked.

f.w: put my life in my hand
f.g: risked my life

n: She urges him to let her feed him so he'll have strength for the journey. Her compassion contrasts with the darkness of the night.

f.g: a bit of food

n: Saul refuses at first, but his servants and the woman insist, and he finally gets up and sits on the couch.

f.g: urged strongly

n: The woman quickly kills a fattened calf and bakes unleavened bread — a generous meal.

f.g: bread made without yeast, quickly prepared

n: Saul and his servants eat, then leave into the night. It is Saul's last meal; his story ends in darkness.
